# Canva Colors & Fonts Reference

Professional color palettes and typography recommendations for designing resumes and documents.

## Professional Color Palettes

Choose one palette and stick with it for visual consistency.

### Palette 1: Classic Blue & Gray (Conservative, Trustworthy)

**Primary**: Navy Blue `#003366` - Section headings, name
**Secondary**: Medium Gray `#666666` - Dates, company names
**Accent**: Light Blue `#0066CC` - Links, highlights
**Background**: White `#FFFFFF` or Very Light Gray `#F5F5F5`

**Best for**: Finance, Law, Healthcare, Corporate roles

**Example usage**:
- Name: Navy Blue, 18pt bold
- Section headers: Navy Blue, 13pt bold
- Dates: Medium Gray, 11pt
- Body text: Black, 11pt

---

### Palette 2: Modern Teal & Green (Creative, Growth-oriented)

**Primary**: Teal `#008080` - Section headings, name
**Secondary**: Forest Green `#2D5016` - Dates, company names
**Accent**: Light Teal `#00CED1` - Links, highlights
**Background**: White `#FFFFFF` or Off-white `#F0F8F8`

**Example usage**:

- Section headers: Teal, 13pt bold

## Font Pairing Recommendations

Combine a sans-serif for body and headers, or pair serif + sans-serif for contrast.

### Modern Combinations (Sans-serif pair)

**Option 1**: Montserrat + Lato
- Headers: Montserrat Bold
- Body: Lato Regular
- Works for: Tech, Design, Creative roles

**Option 2**: Roboto + Open Sans
- Headers: Roboto Bold
- Body: Open Sans Regular
- Works for: Corporate tech, Engineering, Startups

**Option 3**: Raleway + Inter
- Headers: Raleway SemiBold
- Body: Inter Regular
- Works for: Finance tech, Modern businesses

### Traditional Combinations (Serif + Sans)

**Option 1**: Playfair Display + Lato
- Headers: Playfair Display Bold
- Body: Lato Regular
- Works for: Executive, Finance, Luxury brands

**Option 2**: Merriweather + Open Sans
- Headers: Merriweather Bold
- Body: Open Sans Regular
- Works for: Law, Consulting, Traditional businesses

---

## Typography Scale

### Font Sizes for Different Sections

| Element | Size | Weight | Color |
|---------|------|--------|-------|
| Your Name | 18-20pt | Bold | Primary color |
| Contact Info | 10-11pt | Regular | Primary or secondary |
| Section Headings | 13pt | Bold | Primary color |
| Job Title | 11pt | Bold | Black |
| Company/Organization | 11pt | Regular | Secondary color |
| Dates | 11pt | Regular or Italic | Secondary color |
| Location | 10pt | Italic | Secondary color |
| Body Text/Bullets | 10-11pt | Regular | Black |
| Achievements | 10-11pt | Regular | Black |

### Hierarchy Example

```
YOUR NAME (18pt, Bold, Primary)
─────────────────────────────
📧 email@example.com | 📱 (555) 123-4567 | 🔗 linkedin.com/in/you
(10pt, Regular)

EXPERIENCE (13pt, Bold, Primary)
─────────────────────────────

Senior Software Engineer (11pt, Bold, Black)
Tech Company Inc., San Francisco, CA (11pt, Regular, Secondary)
Jan 2021 – Present (11pt, Regular Italic, Secondary)

• Developed microservices architecture (10pt, Regular, Black)
• Increased system performance by 40% (10pt, Regular, Black)
```

## Color Usage Tips

### Do's ✓
- ✓ Use primary color for name and section headings
- ✓ Use secondary color for dates and metadata
- ✓ Limit to 2-3 colors total
- ✓ Maintain contrast for readability
- ✓ Use accent color sparingly (links, highlights)
- ✓ Use white space as design element

### Don'ts ✗
- ✗ Don't use more than 3 colors
- ✗ Don't use neon or highly saturated colors
- ✗ Don't put colored text on colored backgrounds
- ✗ Don't forget about black & white printing
- ✗ Don't use colors that clash (unless intentional)
- ✗ Don't make text hard to read with poor contrast

---

## Contrast Checker

**Recommended WCAG Contrast Ratios:**
- **AAA (Enhanced)**: 7:1 (preferred for body text)
- **AA (Standard)**: 4.5:1 (minimum for accessibility)

**Test color combinations:**
- Black on White: 21:1 ✓✓✓
- Navy Blue on White: 8.6:1 ✓✓✓
- Medium Gray on White: 5.5:1 ✓✓
- Light Gray on White: 1.5:1 ✗✗ (too low)

**Rule of thumb**: If you can't read it easily on screen, it won't print well either.

## Canva Font & Color Settings

### How to Apply in Canva

1. **Fonts**:
   - Click text element
   - Select font from Canva's library
   - Adjust size, weight (bold, italic, etc.)
   - Set color

2. **Colors**:
   - Create a color palette (up to 5 colors)
   - Use consistently throughout design
   - Click color swatch to apply to elements
   - Note: Save custom colors for brand consistency

3. **Brand Kit** (Canva Pro):
   - Set up brand kit with your colors and fonts
   - Applies consistently across all designs
   - Saves time on future resume versions
